digest.component_or_area: grounding scan testing and analyzer integration
propositions: Reusing immutable scan results across test nodes can reduce repeated tool startup and traversal, with measured candidate cohorts showing 24–68% worker-second savings, but pytest-xdist fixtures are worker-local and cannot guarantee cross-worker reuse without explicit artifact caching or distribution changes.

Real external-tool invocations (Semgrep, ast-grep, gitleaks, scc, ctags) must retain at least one concrete boundary test per failure mode class (tool present/absent, timeout, invalid output, rule discovery, evidence accounting) to maintain contractual coverage accounting and fail-mode detection.

Call-local deduplication of OpenGrep YAML validation (source-path keyed cache within _run_opengrep) removes duplicate semgrep --validate invocations without crossing test boundaries or reusing scan results, reducing validation subprocesses from 22 to 10 in a matched experiment.

The measured 57.7-second combined reuse opportunity across five Python-oracle, five mixed-coverage, and three JS Engine-B scan cohorts projects to 176.5 worker-seconds (24.6% lower) on the current 234.24-second baseline if all treatments are applied, but aggregate CI claims require proof of real analyzer presence across all platform/Python version cells.
